subject: Locked-in unit pricing vs burst credit structure for HexaHealth private deployment
messages:
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@hexahealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-26T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify private deployment pricing model and smoothing for spikes

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — HexaHealth is excited about Redwood for private VPC inference. Before we move deeper into procurement, a few pricing questions from finance and infra:

- We run seasonal spikes (telehealth nights) and want capacity that scales without big overpayment. Do you offer a burst credit pool or pre-purchased burst tokens for VPC/on-prem installs?
- We need to understand: locked-in unit pricing (reserved nodes) vs metered per-token billing for private deployments. How do you amortize the platform fee across committed capacity?
- What are the support tiers (response times, included on-call) and how do those map to price?
- For SLAs, we need a clear crediting formula if maintenance windows or failovers impact our production flows.

I attached a CSV with our last 6 months of usage. Procurement also asked for an example invoice that smooths cost across quarters rather than spiky bills. Any worked examples you can share would help.

Can we get a short options summary (2–3 commercial paths) and a recommended choice for a ~200-node equivalent baseline with seasonal burst needs?

Appreciate it —
Raj
Raj Patel
Director, Platform Engineering
HexaHealth

Attachment: hexa_current_usage.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@hexahealth.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-27T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify private deployment pricing model and smoothing for spikes

Raj,

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we want up front. Quick summary of three commercial paths that map to your ask; attached is a worked model (acme_price_model_v2.xlsx):

Option A — Reserved Nodes (predictable):
- Reserved node commitment for baseline (equivalent to 200 nodes), 36-month amortization of platform fee; lower per-node unit cost.
- Burst pool: add-on burst credits (pre-purchased bucket) at a discounted incremental rate; unused burst credits roll forward quarterly (up to 2 quarters) under the smoothing clause.
- Support: Standard (business hours, 24h ticket triage, 8hr P1 SLA optional with retainer).

Option B — Metered + Platform Fee (flex):
- Monthly metered token billing for inference + platform fee (flat per-month line item).
- Invoice smoothing: we can apply a 3-month rolling average to cap month-over-month variance for finance forecasting.
- Burst: automatic autoscale to additional capacity; charge at a premium multiplier for uncommitted burst.

Option C — Hybrid (recommended for HexaHealth):
- Mid-level reserved baseline (12–24 month commit) + smaller burst credit pool included for seasonal spikes.
- Platform fee amortized across committed baseline; platform fee discounting tied to commit size.
- Premium Support tier (24/7 P1 with 2hr response) available as retainer line item; includes 1x on-call rotation seat for escalation.

Crediting for unscheduled downtime: we propose a crediting formula tied to P99 latency degradation and outage minutes. Scheduled maintenance windows are communicated 30 days out and exclude credits if they fall inside the agreed window; unscheduled incidents that violate SLA will be credited pro-rata against the platform fee. We can draft the exact language in the SOW.

Next steps: Markus will sketch a concession ladder (discounts by commit level) and Grace will propose a support retainer figure aligned to your compliance needs. If you can confirm which path (A/B/C) you want as a starting point, we will produce SOW v3 and a sample smoothed invoice.

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com | (415) 555-0118

Attachment: acme_price_model_v2.xlsx (Excel, 72KB)
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@hexahealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@hexahealth.com
Date: 2026-05-28T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify private deployment pricing model and smoothing for spikes

Irene / team,

Thanks for the clear breakdown — Option C looks like the right balance. A few follow-ups from procurement and security:

- Invoice smoothing: we like the 3-month rolling average but need a guarantee that peak months won't push us over budget by more than 15% compared to forecasted baseline. Can you add an overage guard or early-warning credit?
- Downtime credits: we need explicit language for partial credits when a degradation impacts >5% of requests for >15 minutes. Do you have precedent language?
- Platform fee discount: procurement asked whether Redwood will consider a 20% reduction in platform fee if we commit to a 24-month baseline at 250-node equivalent. If not full reduction, what ladder is realistic?
- For support: we require on-call escalation to include a named escalation engineer during onboarding months and a 30-day runbook review. What does that cost?

Procurement attached our vendor playbook for reference. If you can return a redlineable SOW and a sample monthly invoice (smoothed) by end of week, procurement can fast-track approval.

Regards,
Raj

Attachment: acme_procurement_guidelines.pdf (PDF, 180KB)
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@hexahealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-29T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify private deployment pricing model and smoothing for spikes

Raj — appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers and a proposed commercial concession ladder below.

1) Invoice smoothing & overage guard
- We can apply a 3-month rolling average for invoicing. In addition, we will include an overage guard that caps month-over-month bill increases to 15% above the rolling forecast. Overage beyond the 15% cap is billable but we will refund 50% of the excess as one-time credit if the excess was driven by traffic anomaly (we define anomaly with a simple baseline-plus-Z score test; we can put exact thresholds in SOW).

2) Downtime credits
- Proposed language: if degradation impacts >5% of requests for a contiguous 15+ minute window and it is not scheduled maintenance, customer receives a pro-rata credit against the platform fee equal to (impact minutes / total minutes in billing period) * platform_fee. We'll provide concrete examples in the SOW.

3) Platform fee discount ladder (example)
- 12-month commit at 200-node eq: 10% platform fee discount
- 24-month commit at 250-node eq: 18% platform fee discount + 3 months of complimentary burst credits (200K tokens/month)
- 36-month commit at 300-node eq: 25% platform fee discount + 6 months complimentary burst credits and onboarding retainer waived for first 90 days

4) Support & onboarding
- Named escalation engineer during onboarding: included for the first 60 days with Premium Support retainer (monthly retainer fee to be listed in SOW).
- Runbook review: one-time professional services line item (estimated 2–4 days).

Next steps: we will produce SOW-Redwood-Hexa-v3.pdf with the smoothing clause, crediting language, discount ladder, and a sample smoothed invoice. Once you confirm the 24-month/250-node target, we'll lock in the 18% ladder item and send a DocuSign SOW for signature.

Sound good? If so, Irene will route a Draft SOW and the sample invoice into HubSpot for procurement to review.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com | (415) 555-0199

Attachment: SOW-Redwood-Hexa-v3.pdf (PDF, 210KB)
